concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, skills improve through usage; for example, a character gains proficiency in wielding a specific weapon as they use it in combat, which enhances their effectiveness and encourages players to specialize in particular weapon types based on their playstyle.

In broguece, players can enhance their skills by actively using them during gameplay, such as improving their melee combat proficiency as they engage in battles, which encourages players to focus on specific skill sets and develop their characters organically based on their play style.

In the game 'Crawl', skills improve through active use during gameplay, meaning that the more a player uses a specific spell or weapon, the better their character becomes at it. This mechanic encourages players to focus on particular skill sets and strategize around their play style, leading to diverse and specialized character builds.

In cataclysm-bn, skills improve through repeated use, meaning that players must actively engage in actions related to specific skills, such as crafting or combat, to see their proficiency increase. This system encourages players to focus on and develop particular skills based on their playstyle, leading to more personalized character growth.

definition: A game mechanic where individual skills improve through use rather than automatic level-up gains. This creates an organic progression where the character becomes better at what the player actually does, encouraging specialized builds and repeated practice.
exclusion_criteria: Skills that only improve via level-up allocation
Binary skill system (have/don't have) without progression
Skills that are purely cosmetic without gameplay impact
inclusion_criteria: Skills improve through repeated use (use-based progression)
Skill levels affect effectiveness of related actions
Skill training takes time, creating opportunity costs
Skill caps or diminishing returns prevent maxing everything
title: Skill Training System
